controls.label: Feature values x_i
controls.help: Changes the two feature values, which change the predicted labels y_hat_i, then the residuals r_i, the squared residuals r_i^2, and the result SSE.

controls.label: Observed labels y_i
controls.help: Changes the two observed labels, which change the residuals r_i, the squared residuals r_i^2, and the result SSE, without changing the predicted labels y_hat_i.

controls.label: Slope b
controls.help: Changes the predicted labels y_hat_i, then the residuals r_i, the squared residuals r_i^2, and the result SSE.

controls.label: Intercept a
controls.help: Shifts the predicted labels y_hat_i, then changes the residuals r_i, the squared residuals r_i^2, and the result SSE.

explorations.title: A line through both points
explorations.instruction: Predict: how do the residuals and SSE change when the line passes exactly through both observations? Then apply the preset, which sets obs_x, obs_y, slope, and intercept.
explorations.observe: The predicted labels y_hat_i become [1, 3], the residuals r_i become [0, 0], the squared residuals r_i^2 become [0, 0], and the result SSE drops to 0.
explorations.why: Because a = 1 and b = 1 make a + b x_i equal y_i at both feature values, each residual y_i - y_hat_i is 0, so each squared residual is 0 and their total SSE is 0.

explorations.title: A flat line through the same points
explorations.instruction: Predict: with the same observations, how large is SSE when the slope is 0 instead of 1? Then apply the preset, which sets obs_x, obs_y, slope, and intercept.
explorations.observe: The predicted labels y_hat_i become [1, 1], the residuals r_i become [0, 2], the squared residuals r_i^2 become [0, 4], and the result SSE rises to 4.
explorations.why: A slope of 0 makes the prediction constant at a = 1, so the second observation is missed by 2 units; squaring that residual contributes 4 to SSE while the first observation still contributes 0.
